terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to see which way each of the shop's rules goes for today's order.

tasks.title: Warn when stock runs low
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/decisions.js`, make a `let` called `stockNote`. Use `if` and `else` to give it the text `Running low` when `candlesInStock` is fewer than 5, and `Plenty on the shelf` otherwise. Print it.

Check runs your file with other stock counts, including exactly 5, and compares `stockNote` with the task's text letter by letter.
nextSteps: Make `stockNote` with `let` and no value, above the `if`.
Write the `if` with a comparison of `candlesInStock` and 5 in its round brackets.
Give `stockNote` its text in the `if` part and in the `else` part.
Print it, run the file, then change `candlesInStock` at the top and run it again.
hints: An `if` runs the code in its braces only when the condition in its round brackets is true. The `else` part runs otherwise.
Make the variable before the `if`, so it is still there after the closing brace. "Fewer than 5" leaves out 5 itself.
The shape is `if (candlesInStock < 5) { stockNote = '...' } else { stockNote = '...' }`, with the two texts from the task.

tasks.title: Price the shipping
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, make a `let` called `shippingCents` and give it one value with `if`, `else if` and `else`:

- an order whose `totalCents` is 5000 or more ships free (`0`), wherever it goes
- otherwise a `'local'` order pays `250`
- otherwise a `'national'` order pays `495`
- otherwise it pays `1295`

Print it. Check tries big and small orders in every zone, and one exactly on 5000.
nextSteps: Write the question about the total first: only the first true condition runs.
Add an `else if` for each zone, and an `else` for everything left.
Print it and try a big order abroad at the top.
hints: A chain of `if`, `else if` and `else` asks its questions from top to bottom and runs only the first part whose condition is true.
Free shipping holds in every zone, so ask about the total before you ask about the zone. Compare text with `===`, and "or more" includes the equal case.
The chain starts `if (totalCents >= 5000) { shippingCents = 0 } else if (deliveryZone === 'local') { ... }` and goes on the same way.

tasks.title: One candle or many
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make a `const` called `candleWord` with the short form, `? :`. It is the text `candle` when `quantity` is exactly 1, and `candles` for any other quantity, 0 included. Print it.

Check tries several quantities and looks for `?` and `:` in the line that makes `candleWord`.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on the short form.
Write the question first: is the quantity the same as 1?
After `?` put the value for yes, after `:` the value for no.
Print it next to `quantity` and try 1 and 0 at the top.
hints: The short form picks one of two values in a single line, so it can go straight after `const candleWord =`.
Only exactly one takes the single word, so ask with `===`, not with `>`.
The line has the shape `const candleWord = quantity === 1 ? '...' : '...'`, with the two words from the task.

tasks.title: Say when it ships
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, make a `let` called `shipsWhen`:

- `When restocked`, if `candlesInStock` is fewer than the order's `quantity`
- otherwise `Today`, if `hourNow` is before 14
- otherwise `Tomorrow`

Print it. Check tries a short stock early in the day, exactly enough stock, and the hours around 14.
nextSteps: Decide which question comes first: the stock one holds at any hour.
Write the chain with `if`, `else if` and `else`.
Use the comparisons that match "fewer than" and "before".
Print it and try different hours at the top.
hints: Only the first true part of a chain runs. A short stock waits for a restock even at nine in the morning.
Exactly as many candles as the order needs is enough, and 14 itself is not before 14.
The chain starts `if (candlesInStock < quantity) { shipsWhen = 'When restocked' } else if (hourNow < 14) { ... }` and ends with an `else`.
